No. Most of the 2021 loss was in planted pine, but not all of it.

Of the 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss Hansen mapped in 2021 (2.23% of the asset), the MGAP 2021 forest map puts 68.1 ha (about 84%) in planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). Another 13.2 ha (about 16%) falls outside any mapped forest. No loss was in native forest (0 ha).

There is also a separate 37.3 ha of 2021 loss in patches under 0.5 ha. It is not counted as an event, so it is not part of the 81.3 ha, and the evidence doesn't say where those patches sit.

The JRC 2020 reference agrees that 98% of the event area was forest, and a later year was observed, so the loss is corroborated.

This shows where the loss occurred, not why. It doesn't establish deforestation, cause, legality, responsibility, or compliance. Loss in a plantation may simply be harvest.
